posts.author: Danatoth
posts.body:
Ah, the concept of screen resolution, a term bandied about with such regularity in this modern age of digital wonders, deserves a thorough examination, especially if we are to appreciate its true significance. Permit me, therefore, as a humble servant of technological enlightenment, to expound upon this notion with the grandeur and meticulous detail befitting our esteemed discourse.
Screen resolution, my dear Whoopsie_Woggzy, refers to the quantifiable measure of the clarity and detail observable on a display device. It is fundamentally the count of distinct pixels, those infinitesimal dots of illumination, arranged horizontally and vertically across the viewing screen. Each pixel, a portmanteau of 'picture element', constitutes the smallest unit of a digital image, and collectively, these myriad points amalgamate to render the visuals we perceive.
The conventional manner of expressing screen resolution is through a numerical format denoting the pixel count along the horizontal axis followed by that of the vertical axis, separated by an 'x'. For instance, a resolution of 1920x1080, colloquially termed as 'Full HD', delineates 1,920 pixels horizontally and 1,080 pixels vertically, amounting to a total of 2,073,600 individual pixels. This particular resolution has, in recent history, become a prevalent standard, providing a satisfactory blend of visual acuity and manageable data processing requirements.
One must not overlook, however, the plethora of resolutions that span the gamut from the humble to the sublime. At the lower echelons, we encounter resolutions such as 640x480, known as 'VGA' (Video Graphics Array), a stalwart of yesteryear's computing era. Ascending through the hierarchy, we encounter 1280x720, or 'HD', a resolution that heralded the advent of high-definition broadcasting.
Venturing further into the realms of contemporary sophistication, we arrive at 3840x2160, or '4K UHD' (Ultra High Definition), boasting fourfold the pixel count of Full HD, and promising an extraordinary enhancement in image sharpness and detail. Such a resolution is particularly advantageous in larger displays, where the proliferation of pixels mitigates the risk of visible pixelation, thus preserving the integrity of the visual experience.
In contemplating the import of screen resolution, one must consider the concomitant factor of screen size, for it is the interplay between resolution and screen dimensions that ultimately determines the 'pixel density', often expressed in pixels per inch (PPI). A higher PPI denotes a finer granularity of the display, engendering a crisper and more detailed image. This is why, for instance, a resolution that may appear remarkably sharp on a diminutive smartphone display might seem comparatively lackluster on a grandiose television screen.
Moreover, screen resolution extends its influence into the realms of user interface design and content creation, necessitating a meticulous calibration to ensure optimal display across diverse devices. The proliferation of resolutions such as 2560x1440 (QHD) and 5120x2880 (5K) in the domain of professional monitors underscores the escalating demand for unparalleled clarity, particularly in fields such as graphic design, video editing, and gaming.
In summation, the intricacies of screen resolution encompass not merely the numerical dimensions of pixels but extend to a broader understanding of visual fidelity, pixel density, and their practical implications across various applications. It is a testament to the inexorable march of technological advancement, a beacon guiding us towards ever more immersive and captivating visual experiences.
Thus, as we revel in the splendor of our high-resolution displays, let us not forget the profound technical ingenuity that underpins this marvel of modern science. May we continue to celebrate and explore the boundless possibilities that screen resolution affords, with the same fervor and curiosity that have driven human innovation through the ages.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
@Whoopsie_Woggzy
any plugin can change the screensize, and if you have multiple plugins with that option the numbers of the last plugin count.
if changing the screen size in the community plugin has no effect, then there is a second plugin lower that has a different number set there.
That said, changing screen size affects a lot of other things and should not be done unless you know exactly what your're doing.
for example any game using parallax mapping can react badly to changes in screen size and become effectively not playable if the screen size goes higher than the map size.

So...the point I'm trying to get at is a pixel on your monitor is a pixel on your monitor.
If you have an image that can be displayed within the confines of your screen
anywhere
- an image editor, a different video game, whatever - it will look the same when displayed in RPG Maker.
This whole conversation started because you implied images in RPG Maker MV look inherently worse than other game engines, and it's just not possible for some other software to fit multiple pixels of your image into one pixel on your monitor.
I'll leave it up to someone who has experience with drawing on tablets or scanning in their drawings or whatever to help you with that - I expect the best practice is to make the dpi of your drawing match that of your monitor - but if it looks good someplace, then it looks good in RPG Maker.
And if you
can't
fit your good-looking image onto the size of your screen, then it will be larger than your screen in any other game engine also.
